messages:
devon: Heads-up — deploying canary for llm-routing-service in 22:00 UTC window. Plan: open feature flag safety_bell to 1% (warmup) for 15m, then 10% if gates clear. @maria @sam please ack. Release note: routing fallback + kernel tweak. :bell:

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: canary llm-routing-service @ 22:00 UTC. Will emit health pings to #eng-releases-canary every 30s. Auto-ramp policy: 1% -> 10% after 15m when no gate triggers.

maria: ack. Should we pin model version to v3.2-quant? last time v3.3 had perf variance.

devon: yes, pin to v3.2-quant for canary. will include in deploy metadata.

sam: telemetry thresholds suggestion: errorRate > 0.5% or p95 increase > +200ms relative to baseline => rollback. also add circuit hold: if 3 consecutive health pings fail, auto hold flag and notify.

ops-anne: recommend pre-warm KV cache on canary nodes for 10m before starting traffic. Also set cohort drain to 30s on rollback to avoid tail-latency spikes.

devon: command to set flag (internal):
```
cli flag set safety_bell --cohort 0.01 --mode gradual --pin model=v3.2-quant --meta "canary:5955554321"
```

maria: adding to release notes: "safety_bell flag warmup, v3.2-quant pinned, rollback thresholds: err>0.5% / p95 > +200ms / 3 failed pings." Who's taking oncall?

sam: I'll be primary. @ops-anne backup. I'll watch metrics and push rollback if gates trip.

deploy-bot: Canary started at 5955554345. Health pings started (30s cadence).

devon: Observability update @sam: p95 +120ms, errorRate 0.12% — safe so far; proceeding to ramp to 10% at +15m if stable. :thumbsup:

maria: noted. Updating release notes and changelog.

sam: watching. If anything spikes I'll call rollback and pin traffic back to previous route.
